title: The back-to-back tax, measured in the box score
headline_insight: The published back-to-back per-36 box-composite mean is 13.591 versus 13.905 in the rested group, with a separately rounded reported difference of -0.315. This is a raw pooled association, not a causal fatigue estimate.
what_it_means: The reported raw pooled per-36 differences are -0.315 for back-to-backs, -0.217 for 3-games-in-4-days, and -0.193 for 4-in-6. These classes overlap, so neither their counts nor their differences should be added -- a back-to-back that closes a cluster is also a 3-in-4.
how_to_read: The rested baseline is games with >= 2 days rest and no compression; each density class shows its pooled per-36 mean and the delta beneath the baseline.
why_it_matters: A separate ledger receipt reports a -1.73 average scoring-margin contrast: zero-rest minus at least one rest day, across 4732 rows. It is not offensive rating and is not a significance test of these per-36 differences. The outcome, population, and rested-group definition differ. The derived offensive-rating Schedule Fatigue Tax is under review.
caveat: Descriptive only; raw pooled per-36 means, NOT roster/opponent/minutes/home-away adjusted and NOT significance-tested in this module; overlapping classes are not additive.

cited.value: corpus=player_boxscores_2024_25_2025_26; n=4732; avg margin on 0-rest (-1.41, n=856) vs >=1-day rest (0.32, n=3876)
